name: DRINKING WITH THE MONSTER
editorial_article:
"DRINKING WITH THE MONSTER" is a common misinterpretation of the opening lyrics of the track "Monster Monster" by the American rock band The Almost. The band, fronted by Aaron Gillespie—who gained prominence as the drummer and vocalist for the influential metalcore band Underoath—released the song in 2009 as the title track of their sophomore studio album. The song is a driving, guitar-heavy alternative rock anthem that explores themes of self-destruction, internal struggle, and a desperate desire to escape one's own vices.

The actual lyrics, "I'm sick of drinking poison / I'm sick of worrying," are often conflated by listeners into the phrase "drinking with the monster." This metaphorical "monster" represents the psychological and emotional weight the narrator carries. Produced by Aaron Sprinkle, the track showcases The Almost's shift into a mature, southern-tinged hard rock sound, distinguishing them from the post-hardcore origins of its members. The track remains a pivotal piece in the band's discography, illustrating Gillespie’s transition into melodic, introspective rock. By externalizing personal turmoil as a "monster," the song achieves a cathartic energy that resonates with listeners who identify with the struggle for personal redemption. It serves as a reminder of the raw, honest songwriting that defined The Almost's presence in the alternative rock scene of the late 2000s, turning the misheard title into an enduring, albeit unofficial, hook.
